title: A role is evaluated with its declared assignment
situation: Example 19 (the lead reports a cut's outcome in concept terms) failed in every live batch while its scenario handed the lead the finished cut only as files. A diagnostic batch that also gave the lead its declared assignment, a cut brief in concept terms, removed every realization name (0/5 runs named a check, source or function, against 5/5 before); the one remaining name was the file the scenario used to hand over the outcome, cited honestly as the source. In a real cut the lead holds the outcome as its assayers' verdicts, not as a file. The workflow had been working; the evaluation had not given the role its real inputs.
decision: A behavioral evaluation of a role gives that role its declared assignment and the inputs it holds in a real cut, and nothing a real cut would not give it. Example 19 returns to the execution cut, its scenario giving the lead its cut brief and its assayers' verdicts as they returned them. The lead keeps reporting the outcome in concept terms, as the lead concept says. Decisions 0060 and 0061 are withdrawn by this one: no capability record of the outcome and no rerouting of acceptance were needed.
consequences: Every behavioral scenario is checked against its role's assignment when it is written. Whether acceptance should rest on the assayers' verdicts directly is a question on its own merits, not this fix, and is not open now.
